question: are the within-recension identities genuine repetition, or ingestion duplicates?
verdict: 0 of 667. No pair shares a canonical_citation and no pair is two adjacent sequence positions under one parent, so every one joins two distinct printed addresses. 18 pairs sit under one parent at non-adjacent positions (11 YV, 6 AV, 1 RV) -- a refrain repeating inside one adhyaya or hymn, which is repetition, not duplication.

correction_to_CORPUS_D11.committed: by content_sha256 within one text_role: RV 190, SV 349, YV 6, AV 42 = 587 mantras
correction_to_CORPUS_D11.why_they_differ: content_sha256 is byte identity. The ladder also reaches identity after editorial apparatus, accent placement, orthography and word division are set aside. The RV figure agrees exactly because one consistently-spelled edition has nothing below byte identity to find; the SV, YV and AV figures do not, and the 587 understates within-recension repetition by 380 mantras.

correction_to_the_samavedic_characterisa.committed: the Samavedic cases concentrate on Aranya-versus-Uttararcika pairs
correction_to_the_samavedic_characterisa.verdict: wrong segment. 191 of the 204 SV-SV identity pairs join CHANDA to UTTARA -- the Chandas-arcika (Purvarcika) against the Uttararcika -- and only 8 join ARANYA to UTTARA. The Aranya parvan holds 55 of the 1,844 verses, so it could not carry the concentration.
